rules.text: The aim of the event is to evaluate fencing in a safe and friendly manner, according to the principle “hit without being hit”. Similarly to historical rulesets, the competition tests deliberately abstracted skills; it is not a simulation of an unrestricted fight continued to the bitter end. In this sense, every point is treated as a separate “duel” within the framework of the rules below; losing such a duel is indicated by a point awarded against the losing fencer. Our goal is to establish a relative ranking and identify, over the competition day(s), the fencer who proves best in tactical, technical and athletic ability.

An action is **simple** when it is executed in one movement:
- either **direct** (in the same line),
- or **indirect** (in another line).

**Riposte** (thrust/cut back)
A riposte may be **immediate** or **delayed**, depending on the nature and speed of the action. The riposte may be:

rules.text:
- **Simple, direct**
- **Direct riposte**: hits without leaving the line in which the parry was made.
- **Riposte along the blade**: hits by grazing along the blade after the parry.

rules.text_plain: - Simple, direct - Direct riposte: hits without leaving the line in which the parry was made. - Riposte along the blade: hits by grazing along the blade after the parry.

rules.text:
**Simple, indirect**
- **Riposte by disengagement**: hits in the opposite line to that in which the parry was formed.
- **Riposte with a coupé**: hits in the opposite line to that in which the parry was formed, the blade passing over the opponent’s point.

rules.text:
**Compound riposte**
- **Riposte with a doublé**: hits in the opposite line after describing a full circle around the opponent’s blade.
- **Riposte with a one–two**: hits in the same line after first having gone into the opposite line by passing under the opponent’s blade.

Counter-attacks
Counter-attacks are offensive or offensive–defensive actions made during the opponent’s offensive action.

rules.text: Each fencer is responsible for their own weapon. The weapon must be presented in proper condition at the competition: free of burrs and rust, and with any previous tip tape removed. rules.text_plain: Before the start of the bout, the Referee asks the opponents to agree whether grappling holds are allowed during body-to-body fighting in their bout. This must be noted on the score sheet.

rules.text: The start of the bout is signalled by “Play!”. Any movement executed or initiated before the command is not counted.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.subsection: Beginning, stopping and restarting the bout
rules.text_plain: The start of the bout is signalled by “Play!”. Any movement executed or initiated before the command is not counted.

rules.text: The bout stops on the command “Halt!”, except in special situations which modify the regular and normal conditions of the bout (see [GEN-6.10.9], [GEN-6.10.9] as well): [GEN-6.2.4], [GEN-6.2.5], [GEN-6.2.6], [GEN-6.2.7].
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.subsection: Beginning, stopping and restarting the bout
rules.text_plain: The bout stops on the command “Halt!”, except in special situations which modify the regular and normal conditions of the bout (see [GEN-6.10.9], [GEN-6.10.9] as well): [GEN-6.2.4], [GEN-6.2.5], [GEN-6.2.6], [GEN-6.2.7].

rules.text: After “Halt!”, a fencer may not start a new action; only a movement begun before the order remains valid. Everything which occurs afterwards is not valid (but see [GEN-6.10.9], [GEN-6.10.9]).
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.subsection: Beginning, stopping and restarting the bout
rules.text_plain: After “Halt!”, a fencer may not start a new action; only a movement begun before the order remains valid. Everything which occurs afterwards is not valid (but see [GEN-6.10.9], [GEN-6.10.9]).

rules.text: If a fencer stops before “Halt!” and is hit, the hit is valid.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.subsection: Beginning, stopping and restarting the bout
rules.text_plain: If a fencer stops before “Halt!” and is hit, the hit is valid.

rules.text: “Halt!” must also be called if the fencing becomes dangerous, confused or contrary to the rules; if a fencer becomes disarmed (except in wrestling contexts); or if a fencer leaves the piste/arena.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.subsection: Beginning, stopping and restarting the bout
rules.text_plain: “Halt!” must also be called if the fencing becomes dangerous, confused or contrary to the rules; if a fencer becomes disarmed (except in wrestling contexts); or if a fencer leaves the piste/arena.

rules.text: Except in exceptional circumstances, the Referee may not allow a fencer to leave the piste. If a fencer leaves without permission, first-group penalties apply.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.subsection: Beginning, stopping and restarting the bout
rules.text_plain: Except in exceptional circumstances, the Referee may not allow a fencer to leave the piste. If a fencer leaves without permission, first-group penalties apply.

rules.text: Fencers may request the bout to be stopped by raising their hand, for any valid reason (e.g. equipment failure, injury). The bout is considered stopped only when the Referee gives the command “Halt!”.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.subsection: Beginning, stopping and restarting the bout
rules.text_plain: Fencers may request the bout to be stopped by raising their hand, for any valid reason (e.g. equipment failure, injury). The bout is considered stopped only when the Referee gives the command “Halt!”.

rules.text: Actions initiated before the start command or after the stop command are not valid. Initiating an action before “Play!” or after “Halt!” is a first-group disciplinary offence.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.subsection: Beginning, stopping and restarting the bout
rules.text_plain: Actions initiated before the start command or after the stop command are not valid. Initiating an action before “Play!” or after “Halt!” is a first-group disciplinary offence.

rules.text: The Referee may disregard non-valid hits if they can clearly follow subsequent actions.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.subsection: Beginning, stopping and restarting the bout
rules.text_plain: The Referee may disregard non-valid hits if they can clearly follow subsequent actions.

rules.text: If the Referee stops the bout because they believed an earlier hit was invalid and ignored it, but it later becomes clear the earlier hit was valid, the Referee must, if possible, decide taking the first valid hit into account, even if this requires annulling later hits.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.subsection: Beginning, stopping and restarting the bout
rules.text_plain: If the Referee stops the bout because they believed an earlier hit was invalid and ignored it, but it later becomes clear the earlier hit was valid, the Referee must, if possible, decide taking the first valid hit into account, even if this requires annulling later hits.

rules.text: At the end of the pools and every direct elimination bout, before leaving the field of play, fencers check and sign the score sheet kept by the Referee or staff. In team matches this is done by the team captains.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.subsection: Beginning, stopping and restarting the bout
rules.text_plain: At the end of the pools and every direct elimination bout, before leaving the field of play, fencers check and sign the score sheet kept by the Referee or staff. In team matches this is done by the team captains.

rules.text: In case of equipment failure during the bout, the Referee may allow a break of up to 5 minutes (starting when the Referee confirms the failure). This time may be used for repair or replacement and re-checking. If the competitor cannot continue by the end of the break, the Referee may exclude the competitor from that bout. See [ORG-2.3.13].

rules.subsection: Beginning, stopping and restarting the bout

This time may be used for repair or replacement and re-checking. If the competitor cannot continue by the end of the break, the Referee may exclude the competitor from that bout. See [ORG-2.3.13].

rules.text: Fencing at close quarters is permitted so long as the competitors can wield their weapons correctly and the Referee can follow the action.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: Fencing at close quarters is permitted so long as the competitors can wield their weapons correctly and the Referee can follow the action.

rules.text: It is forbidden intentionally to cause body contact to avoid being hit or to push the opponent, except where the fighters have approved the use of gripping and wrestling actions before the bout. In case of such an offence, first-group penalties apply and any hit scored by the fencer at fault is annulled.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: It is forbidden intentionally to cause body contact to avoid being hit or to push the opponent, except where the fighters have approved the use of gripping and wrestling actions before the bout. In case of such an offence, first-group penalties apply and any hit scored by the fencer at fault is annulled.

rules.text: A fencer does not transgress the basic conventions and is not penalised if, by a flèche attack or vigorous advance, they cause body contact even repeatedly, without brutality or violence.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: A fencer does not transgress the basic conventions and is not penalised if, by a flèche attack or vigorous advance, they cause body contact even repeatedly, without brutality or violence.

rules.text: A flèche systematically ending in body contact (as referenced here) must not be confused with a flèche resulting in a shock that jostles the opponent; the latter is intentional brutality and is punished as a second-group offence at all weapons.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: A flèche systematically ending in body contact (as referenced here) must not be confused with a flèche resulting in a shock that jostles the opponent; the latter is intentional brutality and is punished as a second-group offence at all weapons.

rules.text: Conversely, a running flèche (even passing the opponent) without body contact is not forbidden. The Referee must not call “Halt!” too soon so as not to annul a possible riposte. In a running flèche that does not hit the opponent, if the fencer crosses the boundary, they are considered hit (see: leaving the arena).

rules.text_plain: Conversely, a running flèche (even passing the opponent) without body contact is not forbidden. The Referee must not call “Halt!” too soon so as not to annul a possible riposte. In a running flèche that does not hit the opponent, if the fencer crosses the boundary, they are considered hit (see: leaving the arena).

rules.text: Displacement and ducking are allowed, including where the unarmed hand and/or the knee of the rear leg contacts the floor.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: Displacement and ducking are allowed, including where the unarmed hand and/or the knee of the rear leg contacts the floor.

rules.text: Turning one’s back on the opponent during the bout is forbidden. First-group penalties apply and any hit scored by the fencer at fault is annulled.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: Turning one’s back on the opponent during the bout is forbidden. First-group penalties apply and any hit scored by the fencer at fault is annulled.

rules.text: If a fencer covers or moves a valid target surface by blocking or irregular movement, the fencer is penalised by the Referee with first-group penalties as listed in [DIS-4.1.1]–[DIS-4.1.5], [DIS-4.1.9], [DIS-4.3.20], and any hit scored by the fencer at fault is annulled.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: If a fencer covers or moves a valid target surface by blocking or irregular movement, the fencer is penalised by the Referee with first-group penalties as listed in [DIS-4.1.1]–[DIS-4.1.5], [DIS-4.1.9], [DIS-4.3.20], and any hit scored by the fencer at fault is annulled.

rules.text: Gripping and wrestling (grabbing/control/throw/takedown) are permitted within a bout only if both parties consent before the bout starts. If one party does not accept wrestling, no explanation is required. In team matches, each team member decides individually whether they accept wrestling with the given opponent.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: Gripping and wrestling (grabbing/control/throw/takedown) are permitted within a bout only if both parties consent before the bout starts. If one party does not accept wrestling, no explanation is required. In team matches, each team member decides individually whether they accept wrestling with the given opponent.

rules.text: A wrestling action includes any close-quarter action not executed with the weapon (hand/foot/head techniques, holds, disarms, strikes), as well as weapon actions which, instead of direct hitting, aim to manipulate the opponent's body parts. If either opponent did not consent to wrestling, initiating any wrestling action is a first-group offence.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: A wrestling action includes any close-quarter action not executed with the weapon (hand/foot/head techniques, holds, disarms, strikes), as well as weapon actions which, instead of direct hitting, aim to manipulate the opponent's body parts. If either opponent did not consent to wrestling, initiating any wrestling action is a first-group offence.

rules.text: The Referee may stop the bout after prolonged unsuccessful close quarters or wrestling (at the Referee’s discretion). Grabbing an opponent’s momentarily neutralised blade is permitted. A point may be awarded only if the blade grab is brief and is immediately followed by a weapon hit. If no hit results from the grab, the Referee stops without awarding a point. If the initiating party does not neutralise the opponent’s weapon first and receives a hit, the point is awarded against the initiator.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: The Referee may stop the bout after prolonged unsuccessful close quarters or wrestling (at the Referee’s discretion). Grabbing an opponent’s momentarily neutralised blade is permitted. A point may be awarded only if the blade grab is brief and is immediately followed by a weapon hit. If no hit results from the grab, the Referee stops without awarding a point. If the initiating party does not neutralise the opponent’s weapon first and receives a hit, the point is awarded against the initiator.

rules.text: Scoring wrestling actions:
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: Scoring wrestling actions:

rules.text: With a wrestling hold, lifting at least one of the opponent’s feet off the ground. (Throws/takedowns must NOT be completed.)
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: With a wrestling hold, lifting at least one of the opponent’s feet off the ground. (Throws/takedowns must NOT be completed.)

rules.text: Wrestling holds with or without the weapon that prevent the opponent's movement/escape. The Referee judges whether the control position exists and is valid; once the Referee judges the control/dominance requirements are met, they call "Halt!" and award 1 point against the dominated fencer.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: Wrestling holds with or without the weapon that prevent the opponent's movement/escape. The Referee judges whether the control position exists and is valid; once the Referee judges the control/dominance requirements are met, they call "Halt!" and award 1 point against the dominated fencer.

rules.text: A dominance/control judgement is not applicable in positions where the opponent can break out and initiate valid actions, even if, by active effort, the dominating weapon continues to touch the opponent’s target. The Referee judges validity at their discretion.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: A dominance/control judgement is not applicable in positions where the opponent can break out and initiate valid actions, even if, by active effort, the dominating weapon continues to touch the opponent’s target. The Referee judges validity at their discretion.

rules.text: After a takedown, further fighting is not permitted. The Referee calls "Halt!" if either fencer goes to the ground, or if the Referee cannot judge the action, or if dominance cannot be obtained over a prolonged period (Referee's discretion).
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: After a takedown, further fighting is not permitted. The Referee calls "Halt!" if either fencer goes to the ground, or if the Referee cannot judge the action, or if dominance cannot be obtained over a prolonged period (Referee's discretion).

rules.text: A disarm (where one fencer, by intentional close-quarter action, takes the opponent's weapon) is a valid scoring method, except if the disarmed fencer immediately (before "Halt!") controls the opponent's blade and continues wrestling.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: A disarm (where one fencer, by intentional close-quarter action, takes the opponent's weapon) is a valid scoring method, except if the disarmed fencer immediately (before "Halt!") controls the opponent's blade and continues wrestling.

rules.text: If a fencer drops their weapon or falls without opponent intervention, the Referee calls “Halt!”. A hit achieved by a movement that began before the opponent clearly lost their weapon or fell must be considered valid even if it lands afterwards. By sportsmanship, it is improper to initiate a new attack against an opponent who has lost their weapon or fallen; therefore no point is awarded for such a new attack.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: If a fencer drops their weapon or falls without opponent intervention, the Referee calls “Halt!”. A hit achieved by a movement that began before the opponent clearly lost their weapon or fell must be considered valid even if it lands afterwards. By sportsmanship, it is improper to initiate a new attack against an opponent who has lost their weapon or fallen; therefore no point is awarded for such a new attack.

rules.text: When "Halt!" is called, ground gained is held until a hit is awarded. If no hit is awarded, on re-placing on guard both fencers should retire an equal distance to keep fencing distance.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: When "Halt!" is called, ground gained is held until a hit is awarded. If no hit is awarded, on re-placing on guard both fencers should retire an equal distance to keep fencing distance.

rules.text: However, if the bout was stopped because of body contact (and close quarters is not allowed), the fencers are placed on guard so that the fencer who sustained the body contact remains where they were; this also applies if the opponent made a flèche attack even without body contact.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: However, if the bout was stopped because of body contact (and close quarters is not allowed), the fencers are placed on guard so that the fencer who sustained the body contact remains where they were; this also applies if the opponent made a flèche attack even without body contact.

rules.text: If a competitor crosses completely (with both feet) any boundary line of the arena, the Referee must immediately call “Halt!” and must annul everything that occurred after the boundary was crossed.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: If a competitor crosses completely (with both feet) any boundary line of the arena, the Referee must immediately call “Halt!” and must annul everything that occurred after the boundary was crossed.

rules.text: However, a hit by a fencer who steps out with only one foot remains valid if the action began before “Halt!”, even if the fencer subsequently completely leaves the arena.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: However, a hit by a fencer who steps out with only one foot remains valid if the action began before “Halt!”, even if the fencer subsequently completely leaves the arena.

rules.text: If a fencer leaves the piste completely (both feet), only a hit made by the fencer who remains at least one foot inside may be awarded, and only in Longsword-Combat and Longsword-Afterblow (even in case of simultaneous hits). In Longsword-VOR, the convention rules apply.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: If a fencer leaves the piste completely (both feet), only a hit made by the fencer who remains at least one foot inside may be awarded, and only in Longsword-Combat and Longsword-Afterblow (even in case of simultaneous hits). In Longsword-VOR, the convention rules apply.

rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: If a fencer steps completely beyond a boundary (both feet) without having scored a valid hit before exiting: - on the first exit, the fencer receives a warning; - on any further exit in the same bout, the exiting competitor is penalised by a hit against them (the opponent receives one point), even if the competitor was not actually hit.

rules.text: **Accidental stepping out:** no penalty applies where a fencer leaves the boundary not intentionally but due to unexpected events/accidents (e.g. being pushed).
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: Accidental stepping out: no penalty applies where a fencer leaves the boundary not intentionally but due to unexpected events/accidents (e.g. being pushed).

rules.text: The duration of a bout means effective fighting time, i.e. the total of time intervals between "Play!" and "Halt!".
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: The duration of a bout means effective fighting time, i.e. the total of time intervals between "Play!" and "Halt!".

rules.text: Time is controlled by the Referee or a timekeeper. In bouts where the timer is visible to spectators (strongly recommended for finals), the timer must be placed so it is visible to both fencers and the Referee.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: Time is controlled by the Referee or a timekeeper. In bouts where the timer is visible to spectators (strongly recommended for finals), the timer must be placed so it is visible to both fencers and the Referee.

rules.text: A finished bout or relay segment may not be restarted, even if there was a formal error.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: A finished bout or relay segment may not be restarted, even if there was a formal error.

rules.text: In individual pool bouts, a bout ends when any of the following conditions is met:
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: In individual pool bouts, a bout ends when any of the following conditions is met:

rules.text: One fencer reaches the defined number of hits (or in Afterblow: the defined score):
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: One fencer reaches the defined number of hits (or in Afterblow: the defined score):

rules.text: **VOR**: one fencer reaches **5 hits**.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: VOR: one fencer reaches 5 hits.

rules.text:
**Combat**:
- one fencer reaches **5 hits**, or
- if the score reaches 4–4, a decisive hit must be scored before the time limit ends. Double hits are not taken into account (and the fencers remain where they were on the piste).
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: Combat: - one fencer reaches 5 hits, or - if the score reaches 4–4, a decisive hit must be scored before the time limit ends. Double hits are not taken into account (and the fencers remain where they were on the piste).

rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: Afterblow: - one fencer reaches at least 7 POINTS, - due to weighting, the score may exceed 7; - if both fencers reach or exceed 7 points at the same time (simultaneous hits): - if the point difference is at least 1, the bout ends; - if the score is tied, the scores must be reset to 6–6 and a decisive hit must be scored before the time limit ends. Equivalent simultaneous hits are not taken into account (and the fencers remain where they were on the piste).

rules.text: The score sheet records the final score (VN–Dn, where N = winner’s points and n = loser’s points).
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: The score sheet records the final score (VN–Dn, where N = winner’s points and n = loser’s points).

rules.text: Or three minutes of effective fighting time elapses:
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: Or three minutes of effective fighting time elapses:

rules.text: If, when time expires, there is at least a one-hit difference between the fencers’ scores, the fencer with the higher score is declared the winner. The score sheet records the hits/points actually scored in the bout (VN–Dn, where N = winner’s points and n = loser’s points).
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: If, when time expires, there is at least a one-hit difference between the fencers’ scores, the fencer with the higher score is declared the winner. The score sheet records the hits/points actually scored in the bout (VN–Dn, where N = winner’s points and n = loser’s points).

rules.text: If, when time expires, the score is tied, the fencers fence for a decisive hit for up to one minute. **Before restarting fencing**, the Referee draws lots to decide who will be the winner if the score remains tied after the one minute.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: If, when time expires, the score is tied, the fencers fence for a decisive hit for up to one minute. Before restarting fencing, the Referee draws lots to decide who will be the winner if the score remains tied after the one minute.

rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: In this case, the score sheet records the hits/points actually scored during the bout as follows: - VN–Dn, if a decisive hit was scored within the time limit; - V6–D6, or V4–D4, or V2–D2, or V1–D1, or V0–D0, if the winner is determined by drawing lots.

rules.text: An individual direct elimination bout ends when any of the following conditions is met:
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: An individual direct elimination bout ends when any of the following conditions is met:

rules.text: One fencer reaches the defined number of hits (or in Afterblow: the defined score):
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: One fencer reaches the defined number of hits (or in Afterblow: the defined score):

rules.text: **VOR**: one fencer reaches **10 hits**.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: VOR: one fencer reaches 10 hits.

rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: Combat: - one fencer reaches 10 hits; - if both fencers reach 10 points at the same time (simultaneous hits), they must score a decisive hit before the time limit ends. Equivalent simultaneous hits are not taken into account (and the fencers remain where they were on the piste).

rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: Afterblow: - one fencer reaches at least 11 POINTS; - due to weighting, the score may exceed 11; - if both fencers reach or exceed 11 points at the same time (simultaneous hits): - if the point difference is at least 1, the bout ends; - if the score is tied, they must score a decisive hit before the time limit ends. Equivalent simultaneous hits are not taken into account (and the fencers remain where they were on the piste).

rules.text:
Or the defined effective fencing time elapses:
Two three-minute periods (6 minutes of effective fencing time) separated by two one-minute rest breaks.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: Or the defined effective fencing time elapses: Two three-minute periods (6 minutes of effective fencing time) separated by two one-minute rest breaks.

rules.text: In **VOR**, the first period lasts either until three minutes elapse or until one of the fencers reaches 5 hits.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: In VOR, the first period lasts either until three minutes elapse or until one of the fencers reaches 5 hits.

rules.text: If, when the time defined by the rules expires, the scores are tied, the fencers fence for a winning hit for up to one minute. **Before restarting fencing**, the Referee draws lots (coin toss) to decide who will be the winner if the scores remain tied after the additional minute.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: If, when the time defined by the rules expires, the scores are tied, the fencers fence for a winning hit for up to one minute. Before restarting fencing, the Referee draws lots (coin toss) to decide who will be the winner if the scores remain tied after the additional minute.

rules.text: During the one-minute rest break, one person designated before the bout may approach the competitor closely.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: During the one-minute rest break, one person designated before the bout may approach the competitor closely.

rules.text: The points recorded on the score sheet are the points actually scored during the bout.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: The points recorded on the score sheet are the points actually scored during the bout.

rules.text: Each relay in the team match is fenced to 5 hits (5, 10, 15, 20, etc.). Exceptionally, a relay may end with more than 5, 10, 15, etc. if a fencer scores a valid hit at the end of the relay and an additional penalty hit is also awarded; in this case both are counted. The maximum time for each relay is 2 minutes.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: Each relay in the team match is fenced to 5 hits (5, 10, 15, 20, etc.). Exceptionally, a relay may end with more than 5, 10, 15, etc. if a fencer scores a valid hit at the end of the relay and an additional penalty hit is also awarded; in this case both are counted. The maximum time for each relay is 2 minutes.

rules.text: The first two opponents fence until one reaches 5 hits within the 2-minute time limit. The next two competitors then fence within the 2-minute time limit until one reaches 10 hits, and so on, adding five hits to the target score for each subsequent relay.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: The first two opponents fence until one reaches 5 hits within the 2-minute time limit. The next two competitors then fence within the 2-minute time limit until one reaches 10 hits, and so on, adding five hits to the target score for each subsequent relay.

rules.text: If, after two minutes, the target score for the relay has not been reached, the next two competitors continue the match from the score at which it was stopped, and fence within the 2-minute time limit up to the maximum score prescribed for that relay.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: If, after two minutes, the target score for the relay has not been reached, the next two competitors continue the match from the score at which it was stopped, and fence within the 2-minute time limit up to the maximum score prescribed for that relay.

rules.text: The winning team is the team that reaches the maximum of 45 hits, or the team that has scored more hits when time expires.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: The winning team is the team that reaches the maximum of 45 hits, or the team that has scored more hits when time expires.

rules.text: If, when the time for the last relay expires, the score is tied, the competitors fencing the last relay fence for a decisive hit for up to one minute. Before restarting fencing, the Referee draws lots to decide who will be the winner if the score remains tied after the one minute.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: If, when the time for the last relay expires, the score is tied, the competitors fencing the last relay fence for a decisive hit for up to one minute. Before restarting fencing, the Referee draws lots to decide who will be the winner if the score remains tied after the one minute.

rules.text: Each time the fight is interrupted, the fencers may ask how much time remains.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: Each time the fight is interrupted, the fencers may ask how much time remains.

rules.text: A fencer who attempts to interrupt the bout without justification or to prolong interruptions is penalised as a first-group offence.
rules.section: General provisions and rules common to the weapon categories
rules.text_plain: A fencer who attempts to interrupt the bout without justification or to prolong interruptions is penalised as a first-group offence.

rules.text: After the regulated time has expired, the timekeeper must call “Halt!” (or operate an audible signal) to stop the fight, and a hit initiated but landing after time has expired is not valid.

rules.text: If during the bout an injury or other medical issue arises and is certified by the on-duty doctor and/or medical provider, the Referee may allow a break of up to 5 minutes. rules.text: The longsword is a thrusting and cutting weapon.

rules.text: Any cut delivered with the flat, the long or the short edge of the blade, as well as any thrust, is acceptable provided it is executed in such a way that—assuming a sharp weapon—it would cause injury to an unarmoured opponent. rules.text_plain: When judging whether an attack is correctly executed, the following must be considered:

rules.text: A simple attack, direct or indirect, is correctly executed when the extension of the arm and the continuous threatening of the valid target with the point precede the initiation of the lunge or the flèche.
rules.text_plain: A simple attack, direct or indirect, is correctly executed when the extension of the arm and the continuous threatening of the valid target with the point precede the initiation of the lunge or the flèche.

rules.text: A compound attack is correctly executed when, from the presentation of the first feint with the arm extended, the point threatens the valid target continuously without the attacker withdrawing the arm during the successive movements of the attack and the initiation of the lunge or flèche.
rules.text_plain: A compound attack is correctly executed when, from the presentation of the first feint with the arm extended, the point threatens the valid target continuously without the attacker withdrawing the arm during the successive movements of the attack and the initiation of the lunge or flèche.

rules.text: An attack with a step-forward-lunge or a step-forward-flèche is correctly executed when the extension of the arm precedes the completion of the step forward and the initiation of the lunge or flèche.
rules.text_plain: An attack with a step-forward-lunge or a step-forward-flèche is correctly executed when the extension of the arm precedes the completion of the step forward and the initiation of the lunge or flèche.

rules.text: Simple or compound actions, steps or feints executed with the arm bent are not considered attacks but preparations, exposing the fencer to the initiation of an offensive or offensive–defensive action by the opponent.
rules.text_plain: Simple or compound actions, steps or feints executed with the arm bent are not considered attacks but preparations, exposing the fencer to the initiation of an offensive or offensive–defensive action by the opponent.

rules.text: When analysing the fencing phrase to judge priority of the attack, the following factors must be taken into account:
rules.text_plain: When analysing the fencing phrase to judge priority of the attack, the following factors must be taken into account:

rules.text: If the attack is initiated when the opponent is in the “point in line” position (i.e. with the arm extended and the point continually threatening the valid target — longsword: longpoint/langort), the attacker must first deflect the opponent’s weapon. The Referee must ensure that mere blade contact is not considered sufficient to deflect the opponent’s weapon.
rules.text_plain: If the attack is initiated when the opponent is in the “point in line” position (i.e. with the arm extended and the point continually threatening the valid target — longsword: longpoint/langort), the attacker must first deflect the opponent’s weapon. The Referee must ensure that mere blade contact is not considered sufficient to deflect the opponent’s weapon.

rules.text: If the attempt to deflect the opponent’s blade does not find the blade (dérobement / evasion), the right of attack passes to the opponent.
rules.text_plain: If the attempt to deflect the opponent’s blade does not find the blade (dérobement / evasion), the right of attack passes to the opponent.

rules.text: If the attack is initiated when the opponent is not in point in line, the attack may be executed directly or by disengagement, cut-over, or with feints obliging the opponent to parry.
rules.text_plain: If the attack is initiated when the opponent is not in point in line, the attack may be executed directly or by disengagement, cut-over, or with feints obliging the opponent to parry.

rules.text: Continuous forward stepping with the legs crossing constitutes preparation; against such preparation, any simple attack has priority.
rules.text_plain: Continuous forward stepping with the legs crossing constitutes preparation; against such preparation, any simple attack has priority.

rules.text: In compound attacks, feints must be executed correctly, i.e.:
rules.text_plain: In compound attacks, feints must be executed correctly, i.e.:

rules.text: A thrust feint must be shown with the arm extended while continuously threatening the valid target with the point;
rules.text_plain: A thrust feint must be shown with the arm extended while continuously threatening the valid target with the point;

rules.text: A cut feint must be shown with the arm extended such that the blade and the arm form an obtuse angle of about 135°, and the cutting edge threatens the valid target;
rules.text_plain: A cut feint must be shown with the arm extended such that the blade and the arm form an obtuse angle of about 135°, and the cutting edge threatens the valid target;

rules.text: If during the execution of a compound attack the opponent takes the attacker’s blade during a feint, the opponent has the right to riposte.
rules.text_plain: If during the execution of a compound attack the opponent takes the attacker’s blade during a feint, the opponent has the right to riposte.

rules.text: In compound attacks the opponent has the right to stop-hit; however, for it to be valid, the stop-hit must precede the conclusion of the attack by one fencing time, i.e. the stop-hit must land before the attacker begins the final movement of their attack.
rules.text_plain: In compound attacks the opponent has the right to stop-hit; however, for it to be valid, the stop-hit must precede the conclusion of the attack by one fencing time, i.e. the stop-hit must land before the attacker begins the final movement of their attack.

rules.text: Attack by beat or taking of the blade:
rules.text_plain: Attack by beat or taking of the blade:

rules.text: An attack by beat or taking of the blade is correctly executed and retains its priority when the beat is made on the foible (the weaker half), i.e. the half of the opponent’s blade farther from the guard.
rules.text_plain: An attack by beat or taking of the blade is correctly executed and retains its priority when the beat is made on the foible (the weaker half), i.e. the half of the opponent’s blade farther from the guard.

rules.text: In an attack by beat or taking of the blade, when the beat is made on the forte (the stronger half), i.e. the half of the opponent’s blade closest to the guard, the attack must be considered incorrectly executed (parried), and this beat gives the opponent the right to an immediate riposte.
rules.text_plain: In an attack by beat or taking of the blade, when the beat is made on the forte (the stronger half), i.e. the half of the opponent’s blade closest to the guard, the attack must be considered incorrectly executed (parried), and this beat gives the opponent the right to an immediate riposte.

rules.text: Parry:
rules.text_plain: Parry:

rules.text: A parry (or the complete avoidance of the attack) gives the right to riposte. The simple riposte may be direct or indirect; however, to annul any further actions by the attacker it must be executed immediately, without hesitation or delay.
rules.text_plain: A parry (or the complete avoidance of the attack) gives the right to riposte. The simple riposte may be direct or indirect; however, to annul any further actions by the attacker it must be executed immediately, without hesitation or delay.

rules.text: A parry against thrusts aims to prevent the point from arriving on the target area against which the thrust is directed.
rules.text_plain: A parry against thrusts aims to prevent the point from arriving on the target area against which the thrust is directed.

A parry against cuts aims to prevent the hit from arriving on the target area against which the cut is directed. - the parry is correctly executed when it prevents the opponent’s hit from arriving before the offensive action is completed, by closing the line in which the attack would be completed; - if a parry is correctly executed, the opponent’s attack must be considered parried even if, due to blade flexibility, the point nevertheless reaches the target.

rules.text: Priority ends when the strong parts of the weapons meet (including the crossguard), and/or in wrestling actions. If, after contact of the strong parts of the blades, the fencers immediately hit each other, both hits must be annulled. Otherwise, they may separate and continue fencing (under the conventional longsword rules) or transition to wrestling (under the wrestling rules).
rules.text_plain: Priority ends when the strong parts of the weapons meet (including the crossguard), and/or in wrestling actions. If, after contact of the strong parts of the blades, the fencers immediately hit each other, both hits must be annulled. Otherwise, they may separate and continue fencing (under the conventional longsword rules) or transition to wrestling (under the wrestling rules).

rules.text: If within one fencing time only one valid hit occurs, the Referee awards the hit against the fencer who was hit, regardless of its location, force or the manner of execution.
rules.text_plain: If within one fencing time only one valid hit occurs, the Referee awards the hit against the fencer who was hit, regardless of its location, force or the manner of execution.

rules.text: When during a fencing phrase both fencers land hits simultaneously, this is either a simultaneous action or a double hit.
rules.text_plain: When during a fencing phrase both fencers land hits simultaneously, this is either a simultaneous action or a double hit.

rules.text: A simultaneous action results from the simultaneous decision and execution of an attack by both fencers; in this case, the hits exchanged are annulled for both fencers.
rules.text_plain: A simultaneous action results from the simultaneous decision and execution of an attack by both fencers; in this case, the hits exchanged are annulled for both fencers.

rules.text: A double hit, by contrast, results from a faulty action by one of the fencers. Therefore, if there is not one fencing time between the two hits:
rules.text_plain: A double hit, by contrast, results from a faulty action by one of the fencers. Therefore, if there is not one fencing time between the two hits:

Only the fencer who is attacked is counted as hit: - if they make a stop-hit into a simple attack; - if instead of parrying they attempt to evade but do not succeed; - if after a successful parry they pause momentarily, giving the opponent time to renew the attack (redoublement, remise, reprise); - if into a compound attack they stop-hit at an incorrect time; - if, having point in line (longpoint/langort), their blade is deflected by a beat or taking of the blade, and they then attack or re-establish the line instead of parrying the direct hit.

Only the attacker is counted as hit: - if they attack an opponent’s point in line (longpoint/langort) without first deflecting the blade; - if they search for the blade but do not find it (opponent evades) and they continue their attack; - if during a compound attack the opponent takes the blade, the attacker continues, while the opponent ripostes immediately; - if during a compound attack the attacker bends the arm or pauses momentarily, the opponent stop-hits while the attacker continues; - if during a compound attack the attacker receives a stop-hit in time (one fencing time before the final movement begins); - if their original attack is parried and they score by remise/redoublement/reprise while the opponent’s riposte is immediate, simple, in one fencing time, and without withdrawing the arm.

rules.text: The Referee must put the fencers back on guard whenever, in case of a double hit, the Referee cannot clearly determine which side committed the fault.
rules.text_plain: The Referee must put the fencers back on guard whenever, in case of a double hit, the Referee cannot clearly determine which side committed the fault.

rules.text: A hit that occurs beyond one fencing time (a late after-action) is not relevant to the phrase. Such a hit scores no point and does not annul the original hit received.
rules.text_plain: A hit that occurs beyond one fencing time (a late after-action) is not relevant to the phrase. Such a hit scores no point and does not annul the original hit received.

rules.text: Only the Referee decides on hit validity, applying the following fundamental rules.
rules.text_plain: Only the Referee decides on hit validity, applying the following fundamental rules.

rules.text:
When judging the correctness of hits, the following must be considered:
- A hit delivered with a correctly held weapon (two hands) is worth 2 points,
- A hit delivered with a one-handed weapon grip is worth 1 point.
rules.text_plain: When judging the correctness of hits, the following must be considered: - A hit delivered with a correctly held weapon (two hands) is worth 2 points, - A hit delivered with a one-handed weapon grip is worth 1 point.

rules.text: When, within one fencing time, both fencers receive a hit in a fencing phrase, this may be either a simultaneous hit or a double hit.
rules.text_plain: When, within one fencing time, both fencers receive a hit in a fencing phrase, this may be either a simultaneous hit or a double hit.

rules.text: Hits must be considered simultaneous when the Referee cannot clearly determine the temporal order of arrival of the two hits.
rules.text_plain: Hits must be considered simultaneous when the Referee cannot clearly determine the temporal order of arrival of the two hits.

rules.text:
Hits must be considered double when
- both hits occur within the same fencing phrase,
- there is no full fencing-time difference between the two hits, therefore
- the Referee cannot clearly establish that completion of one hit preceded the start of the movement directly delivering the other hit.
- The movement directly delivering the hit may be, for example, a simple (direct or indirect) attack/stop-hit/riposte; or, in a compound attack/stop-hit/riposte, the final motion aimed at the final target.
- Examples (examining action timing, not action priority): stop-hit into a simple attack, or into the final movement of a compound attack, where both actions land.
<!-- **LS-AB-1.2.4**
The Referee’s decision regarding the distinction between simultaneous, double, and after-hits is a finding of fact, which is not challengeable; therefore video refereeing may not be requested.   -->
rules.text_plain: Hits must be considered double when - both hits occur within the same fencing phrase, - there is no full fencing-time difference between the two hits, therefore - the Referee cannot clearly establish that completion of one hit preceded the start of the movement directly delivering the other hit. - The movement directly delivering the hit may be, for example, a simple (direct or indirect) attack/stop-hit/riposte; or, in a compound attack/stop-hit/riposte, the final motion aimed at the final target. - Examples (examining action timing, not action priority): stop-hit into a simple attack, or into the final movement of a compound attack, where both actions land.

rules.text: After-hits
rules.text_plain: After-hits

rules.text:
A hit is considered an after-hit and reduces the value (weight) of the original hit if it is executed as follows:
- **after a fencer has received a valid hit**,
- the fencer lands a hit with an immediate, **simple**, after-action executed without indecision or delay;
- without a clearly perceptible break/separation in the fencing, or a re-evaluation of fencing roles.
- Examples (examining action timing, not action priority):
- a stop-hit lands during a feinted attack, **before the final movement of the attack has begun**, but the attacker finishes the attack (the attack lands outside fencing time and therefore qualifies as an after-hit);
- an after-hit landed with a **simple riposte after a failed parry (received hit)**
rules.text_plain: A hit is considered an after-hit and reduces the value (weight) of the original hit if it is executed as follows: - after a fencer has received a valid hit, - the fencer lands a hit with an immediate, simple, after-action executed without indecision or delay; - without a clearly perceptible break/separation in the fencing, or a re-evaluation of fencing roles. - Examples (examining action timing, not action priority): - a stop-hit lands during a feinted attack, before the final movement of the attack has begun, but the attacker finishes the attack (the attack lands outside fencing time and therefore qualifies as an after-hit); - an after-hit landed with a simple riposte after a failed parry (received hit)

rules.text:
For consistent rule application, the head Referee may determine a clearly perceptible interruption of the fencing phrase based on the following observable events:
- When the Referee perceives the first hit, the bout is stopped; actions initiated after the halt must be annulled, and these belong to first-group disciplinary offences (cf. General / Conduct of the bout).
- A clearly perceptible temporal difference exists if, between the two hits, any of the following is observed:
- clear withdrawal/raising-back of the weapon, or withdrawal of threat
- initiation of the next step instead of/before the after-cut or after-thrust
- a moment when the opponent is no longer under immediate threat
rules.text_plain: For consistent rule application, the head Referee may determine a clearly perceptible interruption of the fencing phrase based on the following observable events: - When the Referee perceives the first hit, the bout is stopped; actions initiated after the halt must be annulled, and these belong to first-group disciplinary offences (cf. General / Conduct of the bout). - A clearly perceptible temporal difference exists if, between the two hits, any of the following is observed: - clear withdrawal/raising-back of the weapon, or withdrawal of threat - initiation of the next step instead of/before the after-cut or after-thrust - a moment when the opponent is no longer under immediate threat

rules.text:
In cases of simultaneous hits AND double hits, both fencers are considered hit. Hits must be awarded as follows:
- if both fencers landed with a two-handed grip, 1 point must be awarded against both fencers
- if both fencers landed with a one-handed grip, 1 point must be awarded against both fencers
- if one fencer landed one-handed and the other two-handed simultaneously, 1 point must be awarded against the fencer who held the weapon one-handed.
rules.text_plain: In cases of simultaneous hits AND double hits, both fencers are considered hit. Hits must be awarded as follows: - if both fencers landed with a two-handed grip, 1 point must be awarded against both fencers - if both fencers landed with a one-handed grip, 1 point must be awarded against both fencers - if one fencer landed one-handed and the other two-handed simultaneously, 1 point must be awarded against the fencer who held the weapon one-handed.

rules.text:
In case of after-hits, the hit must be awarded against the fencer who was hit first in temporal order. The after-hit is not awarded in its own right, but only from the perspective of whether it qualifies as a valid after-hit relative to the first, original hit.
<!-- **LS-AB-1.2.8**
In a double hit, the second hit (regardless of whether executed with one or two hands on the weapon) reduces the number of points awardable relative to the original hit:
- if the original hit is worth 2 points, the second hit reduces the registered score to 1
- if the original hit is worth 1 point, the second hit reduces the registered score to 0.   -->
rules.text_plain: In case of after-hits, the hit must be awarded against the fencer who was hit first in temporal order. The after-hit is not awarded in its own right, but only from the perspective of whether it qualifies as a valid after-hit relative to the first, original hit.

rules.text:
An after-hit (regardless of whether executed with one or two hands on the weapon) reduces the number of points awardable relative to the original hit:
- if the original hit is worth 2 points, the after-hit reduces the registered score to 1
- if the original hit is worth 1 point, the after-hit reduces the registered score to 0.
rules.text_plain: An after-hit (regardless of whether executed with one or two hands on the weapon) reduces the number of points awardable relative to the original hit: - if the original hit is worth 2 points, the after-hit reduces the registered score to 1 - if the original hit is worth 1 point, the after-hit reduces the registered score to 0.

rules.text: Defence against after-actions
rules.text_plain: Defence against after-actions

rules.text:
If the fencer who delivered the original hit **defends with the blade against the actually executed after-action** (the fact of the defence is sufficient; a riposte is not required), the registered score is increased:
- if the original hit is worth 2 points, defending the after-action increases the registered score to 3
- if the original hit is worth 1 point, defending the after-action increases the registered score to 2
rules.text_plain: If the fencer who delivered the original hit defends with the blade against the actually executed after-action (the fact of the defence is sufficient; a riposte is not required), the registered score is increased: - if the original hit is worth 2 points, defending the after-action increases the registered score to 3 - if the original hit is worth 1 point, defending the after-action increases the registered score to 2

rules.text: An after-action started before the halt command may be defended, but any further action initiation after “Halt!”, including a riposte from defending the after-action, still belongs to first-group disciplinary offences.
rules.text_plain: An after-action started before the halt command may be defended, but any further action initiation after “Halt!”, including a riposte from defending the after-action, still belongs to first-group disciplinary offences.

rules.text: Preventing/deflecting hits within one fencing time (e.g. closing cuts/thrusts) is not considered defence against an after-action.
rules.text_plain: Preventing/deflecting hits within one fencing time (e.g. closing cuts/thrusts) is not considered defence against an after-action.

rules.text: Defence against an after-action may be awarded only if it is executed after a valid original hit, against an actual valid after-action, with an actual defensive action: i.e. a new, immediate, actual parry movement executed after receiving/landing the original hit (cf. above: After-hits).
rules.text_plain: Defence against an after-action may be awarded only if it is executed after a valid original hit, against an actual valid after-action, with an actual defensive action: i.e. a new, immediate, actual parry movement executed after receiving/landing the original hit (cf. above: After-hits).

rules.text: The failure or invalidity of an attempted after-action (e.g. too short, misses, falls onto the opponent’s sword) is NOT in itself considered defence against an after-action.
rules.text_plain: The failure or invalidity of an attempted after-action (e.g. too short, misses, falls onto the opponent’s sword) is NOT in itself considered defence against an after-action.

rules.text:
If no actual after-action was executed, defence against an after-action cannot be awarded, not even if
- the fencer who landed the original hit creates blade contact through attack reprise or blade attack.
- the opponent, after being hit, initiates an action that does not qualify as an after-action (delay, interrupted fencing phrase, action initiated after halt).
- Cf. after-hits and their conditions [LS-AB-1.2.5].
rules.text_plain: If no actual after-action was executed, defence against an after-action cannot be awarded, not even if - the fencer who landed the original hit creates blade contact through attack reprise or blade attack. - the opponent, after being hit, initiates an action that does not qualify as an after-action (delay, interrupted fencing phrase, action initiated after halt). - Cf. after-hits and their conditions [LS-AB-1.2.5].

rules.text: If a simultaneous or double hit is followed by an after-hit within the same fencing phrase, the after-hit must be ignored.
rules.text_plain: If a simultaneous or double hit is followed by an after-hit within the same fencing phrase, the after-hit must be ignored.

rules.text: If there is a double hit or hit-after-hit where one is valid and the other invalid (off-target, delivered after leaving the piste, etc.), **only the valid hit must be awarded**, as if it were the original and only hit. If an additional after-hit then occurs (e.g. a reprise after an off-target hit), it must be ignored.
rules.text_plain: If there is a double hit or hit-after-hit where one is valid and the other invalid (off-target, delivered after leaving the piste, etc.), only the valid hit must be awarded, as if it were the original and only hit. If an additional after-hit then occurs (e.g. a reprise after an off-target hit), it must be ignored.

rules.text: If the Referee cannot judge whether an alleged hit occurred or is valid, the hit or double hit is annulled, no point is awarded, and the fencers are reset where the bout was stopped (cf.: 03-general / Ground won or lost).
rules.text_plain: If the Referee cannot judge whether an alleged hit occurred or is valid, the hit or double hit is annulled, no point is awarded, and the fencers are reset where the bout was stopped (cf.: 03-general / Ground won or lost).

rules.text: If the original hit is invalid (off-target, or delivered after leaving the piste, etc.), the subsequent after-hit is not a scoring action, must be annulled, and the fencers must be reset on guard to the on-guard lines.
rules.text_plain: If the original hit is invalid (off-target, or delivered after leaving the piste, etc.), the subsequent after-hit is not a scoring action, must be annulled, and the fencers must be reset on guard to the on-guard lines.

rules.text: Fencers must precisely and honestly comply with the MHS competition rules and statutes, any special rules applicable to the given event, the traditional customs of courtesy and propriety, and the instructions of officials.
rules.section: Disciplinary Rules for Competitions
rules.text_plain: Fencers must precisely and honestly comply with the MHS competition rules and statutes, any special rules applicable to the given event, the traditional customs of courtesy and propriety, and the instructions of officials.

rules.text: They expressly submit themselves to the following provisions based on the principles of order, discipline and sportsmanship. In case of breach, depending on the facts and circumstances, the competent disciplinary authority may apply the prescribed sanctions, with or without a prior warning.
rules.section: Disciplinary Rules for Competitions
rules.text_plain: They expressly submit themselves to the following provisions based on the principles of order, discipline and sportsmanship. In case of breach, depending on the facts and circumstances, the competent disciplinary authority may apply the prescribed sanctions, with or without a prior warning.

rules.text: All persons participating in or present at a fencing competition must respect the MHS Statutes. Everyone must respect order and no one may disrupt the smooth running of the competition. During bouts, no one is entitled to approach the arena, give advice to the fencers, criticise or insult the referee or assistant referee, or attempt to influence them in any way. Even the team captain must remain in the designated place and may intervene only in the cases and manner described in [DIS-1.3.14]. The Referee must immediately stop any conduct that disturbs the smooth conduct of the bout (see [DIS-2.1.2]–[DIS-2.1.4]). Anyone who threatens or insults an official for any reason commits a 4th-group offence and must be sanctioned in accordance with [DIS-4.3.15]–[DIS-4.3.16].

rules.text: Any person who insults or threatens an official for any reason may be immediately disqualified and/or expelled from the premises.
rules.section: Disciplinary Rules for Competitions
rules.text_plain: Any person who insults or threatens an official for any reason may be immediately disqualified and/or expelled from the premises.

rules.text: The Referee and/or the Organising Team may, within their own authority, decide to expel from the competition area any person whose gestures, behaviour or language disrupt the orderly running of the competition.
rules.section: Disciplinary Rules for Competitions
rules.text_plain: The Referee and/or the Organising Team may, within their own authority, decide to expel from the competition area any person whose gestures, behaviour or language disrupt the orderly running of the competition.

rules.text: By the mere fact of their participation, fencers pledge on their honour that they will comply with the rules; submit to the decisions and instructions of officials; treat the Referees (referees and assistant referees) with respect; and conscientiously follow their instructions and decisions.
rules.section: Disciplinary Rules for Competitions
rules.text_plain: By the mere fact of their participation, fencers pledge on their honour that they will comply with the rules; submit to the decisions and instructions of officials; treat the Referees (referees and assistant referees) with respect; and conscientiously follow their instructions and decisions.

rules.text: A fencer may not take part in the competition if they refuse to fence another competitor who is properly entered for the event. Breach of this rule must be sanctioned as set out in the 4th group of disciplinary offences.
rules.section: Disciplinary Rules for Competitions
rules.text_plain: A fencer may not take part in the competition if they refuse to fence another competitor who is properly entered for the event. Breach of this rule must be sanctioned as set out in the 4th group of disciplinary offences.

rules.text: Fencers must appear at the specified place and time for their pool round, bout or direct elimination bout, and at the designated equipment-check time before their bout, fully equipped in conformity with the rules and ready to fence, and whenever the Referee calls them to do so during the competition.

rules.text: When presenting themselves to start a bout, fencers must enter the arena fully ready to fence — in regulation clothing, jacket closed, glove on, and weapon in hand.
rules.section: Disciplinary Rules for Competitions
rules.text_plain: When presenting themselves to start a bout, fencers must enter the arena fully ready to fence — in regulation clothing, jacket closed, glove on, and weapon in hand.

rules.section: Disciplinary Rules for Competitions
rules.text_plain: If during the competition a fencer does not appear in the arena when called by the Referee: - The absent fencer receives a yellow card; - One minute after the first call, they are called a second time; if still absent, the fencer receives a red card; - One minute after the second call, they receive a third and final call; continued absence results in exclusion from the event.

rules.text: Competitors must fence honestly and in strict compliance with this ruleset. Any breach entails the sanctions recorded here.
rules.section: Disciplinary Rules for Competitions
rules.text_plain: Competitors must fence honestly and in strict compliance with this ruleset. Any breach entails the sanctions recorded here.

rules.text: Every bout must remain courteous and honest. Any irregular action (a flèche that ends by pushing the opponent, confused/disorderly fencing, irregular movements, violent hits, punches, kicks, hitting with a basket/crossguard, deliberately falling to avoid being hit) or unsportsmanlike behaviour is expressly forbidden — see also [DIS-4.1.1]–[DIS-4.1.5], [DIS-4.3.20]. If such an offence arises, any hit scored by the fencer at fault must be annulled.

rules.text: Before the start of a bout, the two fencers salute (fencing salute) their opponent, the Referee and the audience. rules.text:
The overall ranking table is formed as follows:
- Compute the two indices (V/M, HS–HR) by aggregating the pool summary values.
- The primary index is computed as victories divided by matches, per the V/M formula.
- The fencer with the highest index (maximum 1) takes first place.
- If multiple fencers have the same primary index, the secondary index HS–HR is used to rank them, i.e. hits scored minus hits received.
- If both indices are equal, the fencer who scored more hits is ranked higher.
- In case of absolute equality between two or more fencers, the order is determined by drawing lots.

rules.text:
